rationale: Docs-vs-code final truth pass. I sampled 30+ documented claims across the 12 domain docs, the 2 guides, the 2 templates, and the 4 ADR amendments, and checked each against the landed code at 8eaeb05e. The documentation on this branch is unusually accurate: every exported signature in core/interfaces.md (8 of them) and workflow/interfaces.md matches the Go declaration exactly; every verbatim-quoted string I checked (IgnoredDirtNotice's notice text, the emit-only bypass line, panel/gate.go's 'materialize them into a commit past review' refusal) matches byte for byte; ADR-0023's struck-row amendment is correct against the shipped DerivePhaseFromChildren including its blocked-child reasoning; ADR-0025 R5.1's two containment-gated classes match ComputeEntangleablePaths exactly (including the HasGitignoreEntry/EnsureGitignoreEntry pairing and the step-7.5 recording writes); ADR-0037's amendment is correct and correctly scoped ('retired from this path', not globally -- CommitAll legitimately survives at the commitWithExport funnel); ADR-0041's M/R/S protocol, marker ref, CAS semantics, Mindspec-Stage trailer, and re-entry discriminator all match materialize.go, and its reconcile-authors-no-commits claim holds (runMaterialization is the sole call site, complete.go:909). The agreement table's guide half and fixture half agree cell for cell across all 13 rows, and TestAgreementTable_* is green. `mindspec validate docs` reports zero errors at the tip (only the pre-existing missing-source-globs WARN the BRIEF names as out of scope). The four ADR amendments read as a coherent set with the new domain docs. I found no case where a document overstates what the code does at the mechanism level. What I did find is six text-level defects, all doc-only, none touching code correctness. One is a genuine cross-document contradiction about operator recovery (F1): workflow/runbook.md tells an operator that a single --allow-doc-skew 'is the whole recovery' for a gate-refused complete, which is precisely the claim merge-safety.md -- landed in the same bead-10 sweep -- was written to refute, and which the code contradicts (materialize.go runs doc-sync and the ADR gate sequentially, so --allow-doc-skew alone can surface a fresh ADR-divergence refusal). Two are dead pointers in lifecycle-modes.md (F2, F3) -- one lands on a bare closing brace, the other on a different function's doc comment entirely. In a spec whose whole thesis is that reported state must not overstate observed state, guidance that overstates a recovery and citations that point at nothing are the same defect class this branch exists to close, so I am filing REQUEST_CHANGES rather than waving them through as nits. All six fixes are mechanical text edits; none requires a code change, a re-panel of any bead, or a re-run of any gate.
concrete_changes_required: F1 (primary) -- .mindspec/domains/workflow/runbook.md, 'Lifecycle-verb behaviour changes an operator will notice (spec 128)' item 1: replace 're-running the same command with the appropriate override (`--allow-doc-skew "<reason>"`) is the whole recovery' with wording consistent with project-docs/user/guides/merge-safety.md's 'Gate-refused `mindspec complete` converges on a plain retry' section, which explicitly states the opposite ('Neither override is "the whole recovery" on its own when both classes of skew are present'). The item names BOTH content gates (doc-sync, ADR-divergence) but offers only --allow-doc-skew, so an ADR-divergence refusal is given the wrong recovery flag. Code confirms merge-safety.md and refutes the runbook: internal/complete/materialize.go:271-283 runs ValidateDocsSnapshot (gated on opts.AllowDocSkew) and only then CheckADRDivergenceSnapshot/handleADRGateOutcome, so --allow-doc-skew alone can surface a fresh ADR-divergence refusal. Suggested: '...re-running after fixing the skew, or with the override for the gate that refused (`--allow-doc-skew "<reason>"` for doc-sync, `--override-adr "<reason>"` for ADR-divergence), is the recovery -- the two gates run sequentially, so overriding one can surface the other; see merge-safety.md for the full two-retry contract.'

F2 -- project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md line 47: the citation '`phase.DerivePhaseWithStatus`-class, `derive.go:166`/`:174`' is stale. DerivePhaseWithStatus is at internal/phase/derive.go:182 and DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache at :190; line 166 is a comment line inside DerivePhase's doc block ('// hot-path callers should use DerivePhaseWithCache to share bd queries.') and line 174 is a bare '}'. Both are off by 16. Fix by dropping the line numbers and citing the function names (`DerivePhaseWithStatus`/`DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache` in `derive.go`), which cannot go stale on an unrelated edit above them.

F3 -- project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md line 172 (Writer taxonomy, disclosed-residual bullet): the citation '`complete.go:1398-1420`' for completeSyncPhase's doc comment points at the wrong function. completeSyncPhase's doc comment is internal/complete/complete.go:1297-1332 (the residual specifically at 1311-1332; func at 1333); lines 1398-1420 are inside advanceState's doc comment, which says nothing about the plan-over-implement residue. The SUBSTANCE of the guide's claim is fully accurate -- the comment at 1311-1332 records exactly the residual described, in matching detail -- only the pointer is wrong. Fix by citing `completeSyncPhase`'s doc comment (complete.go:1311-1332) or the function name alone.

F4 -- .mindspec/domains/core/architecture.md, 'The `mindspec_phase` write lock...' section: the sentence 'Every writer of an epic's `mindspec_phase` metadata key -- <eight named sites> -- now executes inside `phase.WithPhaseWriteLock(...)`' reads as an exhaustive inventory but omits cmd/mindspec/next.go:608's advancePhaseOnClaim, a mindspec_phase writer THIS spec added (bead 7's claim-time advance, writing {"mindspec_phase": state.ModeImplement}). The universal claim itself stays TRUE (that writer does execute inside the lock, and writer_inventory_test.go's AST walk over cmd/ and internal/ covers it structurally without naming sites), so this is an incomplete inventory rather than a false statement -- but the omitted writer is exactly the b2<->b7 seam the final-review BRIEF flags as suspect, and two sibling documents do name it (workflow/architecture.md's R6 section: 'cmd/mindspec/next.go also gained a new mindspec_phase writer under the R3.3 lock'; lifecycle-modes.md's writer taxonomy, which classifies it as evidence-fresh forward-by-intent). Add `cmd/mindspec/next.go`'s `advancePhaseOnClaim` to the enumeration. Same omission in .mindspec/domains/core/overview.md's 2026-09-03 note, whose consuming-verbs list ('`repair phase`, `plan approve`, `spec approve`, `complete`, `release`, `impl approve`/`adopt`') likewise leaves out `next`.

F5 (nit) -- project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md lines 24-27: 'for the eight rows whose canonical epic fixture carries a stored phase -- `phase.DerivePhaseFromChildren` run directly on the fixture's children'. The COUNT is right (seven assertChildDerivation call sites at agreement_table_test.go:552/571/594/623/640/659/677, plus row 12's own DerivePhaseFromChildren check at :849 = eight), but the stated selection CRITERION is wrong: the terminal row and the repair-phase v2 row also carry seeded stored phases and have no such leg -- the test file states explicitly that the terminal row has no children-only leg by design, because bare DerivePhaseFromChildren cannot express 'done' for an all-closed set. Reword to the actual criterion, e.g. 'for the seven ordinary three-surface rows plus the forced-backward row'.

F6 (nit) -- .mindspec/domains/execution/architecture.md and internal/executor/executor.go:287 both describe ResetIndexToHead as running '`reset --mixed HEAD`', while ADR-0041 says '`reset --quiet --mixed`'. The actual command is `git reset --quiet --mixed HEAD` (internal/gitutil/materialize.go:238). Not a contradiction -- just a dropped flag in the less-detailed rendering; add `--quiet` for consistency with the ADR, or leave as-is if the flag is deliberately treated as cosmetic.

findings.title: workflow/runbook.md contradicts merge-safety.md on the gate-refusal recovery, and names only one of the two override flags
findings.evidence: runbook.md item 1: 're-running the same command with the appropriate override (--allow-doc-skew "<reason>") is the whole recovery'. merge-safety.md, landed in the same bead-10 sweep: 'Neither override is "the whole recovery" on its own when both classes of skew are present -- passing both flags (or fixing one and overriding the other) is what a fully-skewed worktree needs', and '--allow-doc-skew alone can still surface a fresh ADR-divergence refusal that never ran before'. Code settles it for merge-safety.md: internal/complete/materialize.go:271-283 gates on docResult/opts.AllowDocSkew first, then runs CheckADRDivergenceSnapshot/handleADRGateOutcome. The runbook item also names both gates (doc-sync, ADR-divergence) while offering only --allow-doc-skew, never --override-adr. Operator-facing, and on a path this run itself hit repeatedly (the BRIEF records eight --allow-doc-skew debts paid by bead 10).

findings.title: lifecycle-modes.md cites derive.go:166/:174 for the status-aware derivation; both lines are something else
findings.evidence: Guide line 47 cites 'derive.go:166/:174'. Actual: DerivePhaseWithStatus at internal/phase/derive.go:182, DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache at :190. Line 166 is the comment '// hot-path callers should use DerivePhaseWithCache to share bd queries.'; line 174 is a bare closing brace. Off by 16 in both cases -- consistent with the citation predating ~16 lines of additions above it.

findings.title: lifecycle-modes.md's disclosed-residual citation points at a different function's doc comment
findings.evidence: Guide line 172 cites 'complete.go:1398-1420' for completeSyncPhase's residual-recording doc comment. completeSyncPhase's comment is at internal/complete/complete.go:1297-1332 (residual at 1311-1332, func at 1333); 1398-1420 is inside advanceState's doc comment, which discusses child-status derivation and AC-4b, not the plan-over-implement residue. The claim's substance is accurate against the real comment -- the pointer is not.

findings.title: core/architecture.md's mindspec_phase writer inventory omits next.go's claim-time writer added by this same spec
findings.evidence: core/architecture.md enumerates eight writers after 'Every writer of an epic's mindspec_phase metadata key --'; cmd/mindspec/next.go:608 (advancePhaseOnClaim, writing {"mindspec_phase": state.ModeImplement} inside WithPhaseWriteLock) is not among them, nor in core/overview.md's consuming-verbs list. workflow/architecture.md and lifecycle-modes.md's writer taxonomy both DO name it. The universal lock claim remains true and writer_inventory_test.go's AST walk covers the site structurally, so this is inventory incompleteness, not a false invariant -- but the omitted writer is the b2<->b7 seam the BRIEF flags as suspect, and it is the one writer whose forward/backward classification lifecycle-modes.md needed a dedicated taxonomy bullet to justify.

findings.title: lifecycle-modes.md mis-states which rows carry the stored-independent DerivePhaseFromChildren leg
findings.evidence: Guide: 'the eight rows whose canonical epic fixture carries a stored phase'. Count is correct (7 assertChildDerivation sites + row 12's check at agreement_table_test.go:849), criterion is not: the terminal row seeds state.ModeDone and the repair-v2 row seeds a legacy 'implement', and neither has the leg -- the test file states the terminal row deliberately has none because bare DerivePhaseFromChildren cannot express 'done'.

findings.title: ResetIndexToHead described without --quiet in the execution doc and the Executor interface comment
findings.evidence: execution/architecture.md and internal/executor/executor.go:287 say 'reset --mixed HEAD'; ADR-0041 says 'reset --quiet --mixed'; internal/gitutil/materialize.go:238 runs `git reset --quiet --mixed HEAD`. Detail-level omission only -- all three agree it is an index-only mixed reset to HEAD.

findings.title: Verified clean: exported-signature fidelity across both interfaces docs
findings.evidence: All eight core/interfaces.md phase declarations match exactly (PhaseLockRelPath, ErrPhaseLockTimeout, WithPhaseWriteLock, DescribeLockFailure, SetLockWaitForTest, IsBackwardMove, SanctionedDerivedSync, PhaseSemanticsV2MarkerKey/Value, LegacyPhaseSignature, EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2, DerivePhaseWithStatus(WithCache)), including the documented 10s default (phaselock.go:65). workflow/interfaces.md likewise: ComputeEntangleablePaths(repoRoot, cwd, specID), CheckDirtyTreeProportional(repoRoot, cwd, specID) (blockingDirt, ignoredDirt []string, err error), ReadySet{Filtered, Raw, SpecFlag} with ExcludedCount/ExclusionNotice, BuildReadySet, SelectWork, SelectNamedFromReadySet, IsDraftSpecWithCache, EntangleableClaimPaths/SetEntangleableClaimPathsForTest -- all exact. The documented caller fences hold: SanctionedDerivedSync has exactly one production caller (cmd/mindspec/release.go:167).

findings.title: Verified clean: the four ADR amendments are coherent with each other and with the domain docs
findings.evidence: ADR-0023's two struck rows are correct against DerivePhaseFromChildren (derive.go:399-443): some-closed+some-open+none-in_progress derives implement, and a blocked child counts as neither closed nor in_progress, so the mixed shape lands on the same amended row -- matching the agreement table's row-5 note and its blocked-sibling fixture. ADR-0037's amendment matches gate.go:299's refusal string verbatim and is correctly scoped ('retired from this path'), since gitutil.CommitAll legitimately survives at the commitWithExport funnel per the pre-existing execution doc. ADR-0041's protocol matches materialize.go end to end: snapshot-then-gate-then-materialize ordering, marker CAS with '' for CREATE, the Mindspec-Stage trailer read never inferred, the four-leg re-entry discriminator, and the pre-S/at-tree S-stage classification refusing before MaterializeStageCommit. The code carries one leg the ADR does not enumerate (a corrupt/unknown-trailer marker cleared and treated as absent, materialize.go:132-144) -- a superset of the documented behavior, strictly safer, not a divergence. ADR-0041's reconcile claim holds: runMaterialization is called once (complete.go:909) and no CommitAll/CommitPaths remains on either complete path. ADR-0025 R5.1 matches ComputeEntangleablePaths exactly, including containment gating, the HasGitignoreEntry/EnsureGitignoreEntry write-decision pairing (pinned by TestHasGitignoreEntry_MatchesEnsureGitignoreEntryWriteDecision), the recording step at next.go:389-394, and the stderr notice at next.go:196-198.

findings.title: Verified clean: the agreement table's guide half and fixture half agree, and the docs gate is green

Verbatim strings match byte for byte: IgnoredDirtNotice's 'note: claiming despite unrelated dirty path(s) this claim does not touch (not blocked -- ADR-0025 R5.1): ' (guard.go:552+) and the emit-only bypass line 'emit-only: bead fetched by ID; readiness not checked.' (next.go:478). The two templates' referenced surfaces exist and are cobra-pinned (adoptCmd's --reason via frozen_contract_guidance_test.go; the termsafe template func at instruct.go:39). Execution-domain claims all hold: eight Executor methods present, internal/complete imports no gitutil symbol, MindspecStageTrailerKey/StageMaterialization/StageArtifactSync, bdStderrExcerptLineCap=20, .mindspec/phase.lock in gitignore.go's RuntimeIgnoreEntries, harness/sandbox.go, bootstrap's starterGitignore, and the root .gitignore. `mindspec validate docs` at the tip: zero errors, one pre-existing missing-source-globs WARN (the one the BRIEF names as out of scope).

findings.title: Not a defect: an internal/instruct FAIL I produced was my own test contention, not a branch problem
findings.evidence: Reporting so no one chases it. I briefly ran two overlapping `go test` jobs that both included ./internal/instruct/; that run reported FAIL at 600.216s -- exactly go test's default 10m timeout, with an os/exec goroutine dump rather than an assertion failure. Re-run alone with -timeout 25m, `go test ./internal/instruct/ -short -count=1` passes in 314s. ./internal/resolve passes in 3.6s, and the targeted cmd/mindspec pins (FrozenContract, EmitInstruct) pass. Worth noting for whoever owns the gate, though it is R8's lens not mine: -short internal/instruct at 314s leaves under 2x headroom against the default 10m timeout, so it is a plausible future flake source under CI load.
